    - name: app_reporting__user_value_segmentation_report
      description: RFM-based customer segment report with global aggregation, contribution analysis, growth prioritization, tactical recommendations, and a generation timestamp
      grain: One row per customer_segment
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_user_rfm_analysis
      business_logic: '1) Start from intermediate.int_user_rfm_analysis filtered to data_quality_flag = ''Valid''. 2) customer_segment_overview: group by (customer_segment, buyer_country) and compute per group: - customer_count: distinct customers (app_id). - avg_rfm_score. - total_revenue (sum of monetary_value), avg_customer_value (average monetary_value), median_customer_value (median monetary_value). - total_estimated_clv (sum) and avg_estimated_clv (average). - Behavioral means: recency_days, frequency_count, customer_lifetime_days, avg_transaction_value. - Averages of subscription_count, purchase_count, refund_count. - Health and flags: healthy_customers (status = ''Healthy''), critical_customers (status = ''Critical''), high_value_customers (sum of is_high_value_customer), churn_risk_customers (sum of is_churn_risk), recent_customers (sum of is_recent_customer). 3) global_segment_metrics: aggregate customer_segment_overview by customer_segment: - global_customer_count: sum of per-country customer_count (a customer in multiple countries is counted in each country). - global_segment_revenue: sum of total_revenue. - global_avg_clv: unweighted average of the per-country avg_estimated_clv values. - global_avg_rfm_score: unweighted average of the per-country avg_rfm_score values. - countries_present: number of distinct buyer countries. - largest_country_customer_count: maximum customer_count observed across its countries. - total_healthy/critical/high_value/churn_risk_customers: sums of the respective counts. - health/critical/high_value/churn_risk rate percentages: 100 × summed numerator divided by summed customer_count; if the denominator is zero, return NULL; no rounding. 4) revenue_contribution_analysis: from global_segment_metrics compute: - revenue_contribution_percentage: 100 × segment revenue divided by total revenue across all segments; no rounding; if total is zero, result follows engine behavior. - revenue_rank: row number when ordering segments by revenue descending; ties receive arbitrary distinct ranks. 5) rfm_score_distribution: group rfm_base by customer_segment and compute: - avg_recency_score, avg_frequency_score, avg_monetary_score, avg_rfm_score. - premium_rfm_customers: number of rows with rfm_score ≥ 10 (rows with NULL rfm_score are not counted). - rfm_score_stddev: sample standard deviation of rfm_score; NULL if fewer than two rows. 6) segment_growth_potential: left join global_segment_metrics to revenue_contribution_analysis and rfm_score_distribution, and derive: - growth_potential: High Growth Potential if health_rate_percentage ≥ 80 and global_avg_clv > 300; Medium Growth Potential if health_rate_percentage ≥ 60 and global_avg_clv > 150; Stable Segment if health_rate_percentage ≥ 40; otherwise Declining Segment. - investment_priority by customer_segment: Champions/Loyal Customers → Maintain & Expand; Potential Loyalists → Develop & Nurture; New Customers → Onboard & Engage; At Risk → Immediate Attention; Cannot Lose Them → Win Back Campaign; Hibernating → Reactivation Program; Lost → Evaluate ROI; others → Monitor. - roi_expectation: High if global_avg_clv > 500; Medium if > 200; Low if > 50; otherwise Uncertain. - Carry revenue_contribution_percentage, revenue_rank, and use rfm_score_distribution.avg_rfm_score as segment_avg_rfm_score. 7) final_report: join segment_growth_potential to global_segment_metrics and rfm_score_distribution; select output fields and compute: - recommended_actions by customer_segment: Champions → "Reward loyalty, ask for referrals, offer new products"; Loyal Customers → "Upsell higher value products, recommend based on purchase history"; Potential Loyalists → "Offer membership/loyalty program, recommend popular products"; New Customers → "Provide onboarding support, provide education, start building relationship"; At Risk → "Send personalized emails, offer limited time offers, provide helpful resources"; Cannot Lose Them → "Reach out via phone, offer renewal discounts, provide quality customer service"; Hibernating → "Offer other product categories, special discounts, share valuable resources"; Lost → "Revive interest with relevant products, ignore otherwise"; others → "Monitor and assess". - business_impact_level with precedence: High Impact - Large revenue at risk if revenue > 10000 and health_rate_percentage < 50; else High Impact - Significant growth opportunity if revenue > 5000 and growth_potential is High Growth Potential; else Medium Impact - Substantial customer base if global_customer_count > 100; otherwise Low Impact - Monitor for changes. - report_generated_at: the query execution timestamp with time zone. 8) The final result has one row per customer_segment and is output ordered by revenue_rank, then by revenue descending (ordering does not affect the model grain).'
      columns:
      - name: customer_segment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: RFM segment label from source; grouping key and unique per output row
        tests:
        - not_null
        - unique
      - name: global_customer_count
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Sum across countries of the distinct-customer counts for the segment; customers active in multiple countries are counted in each country
      - name: global_segment_revenue
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,2)
        description: Total segment revenue summed over all valid rows
      - name: global_avg_clv
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Unweighted average of the per-country average estimated CLV for the segment
      - name: revenue_contribution_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 'Segment revenue share: 100 times segment revenue divided by total revenue across all segments; no rounding; engine behavior if total is zero'
      - name: revenue_rank
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Row number when ordering segments by revenue descending; ties get arbitrary distinct ranks
      - name: segment_avg_rfm_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average RFM score across all valid rows in the segment
      - name: health_rate_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 100 times summed healthy customers divided by summed customer_count within the segment; NULL if denominator is zero; no rounding
      - name: critical_rate_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 100 times summed critical customers divided by summed customer_count within the segment; NULL if denominator is zero; no rounding
      - name: high_value_rate_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 100 times summed high-value customers divided by summed customer_count within the segment; NULL if denominator is zero; no rounding
      - name: churn_risk_rate_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 100 times summed churn-risk customers divided by summed customer_count within the segment; NULL if denominator is zero; no rounding
      - name: countries_present
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of distinct buyer countries present in the segment
      - name: largest_country_customer_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Maximum per-country distinct-customer count observed within the segment
      - name: avg_recency_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average recency score across all valid rows in the segment
      - name: avg_frequency_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average frequency score across all valid rows in the segment
      - name: avg_monetary_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average monetary score across all valid rows in the segment
      - name: premium_rfm_customers
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Number of rows in the segment with RFM score ≥ 10; rows with NULL RFM score are not counted
      - name: rfm_score_stddev
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Sample standard deviation of RFM score in the segment; NULL if fewer than two rows
      - name: growth_potential
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Growth category based on health_rate_percentage and global_avg_clv thresholds with defined precedence
      - name: investment_priority
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Investment recommendation mapped from customer_segment labels with a default of Monitor
      - name: roi_expectation
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: ROI expectation based on global_avg_clv thresholds (>500 High, >200 Medium, >50 Low, else Uncertain)
      - name: recommended_actions
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Tactical actions mapped from customer_segment labels with a default of Monitor and assess
      - name: business_impact_level
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Impact category determined by revenue and health thresholds, then by customer count, else low impact
      - name: report_generated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Execution timestamp captured at query time with time zone
        tests:
        - not_null
    - name: app_reporting__app_health_monitoring_report
      description: Daily app health monitoring report with platform benchmarks, rankings, alerts, and final assessment per app-day-platform
      grain: One row per date_day, app_name, platform
      source_models:
      - intermediate.int_app_health_metrics
      business_logic: '- Filter source rows to data_quality_flag = ''Valid'' (base set: app_health_base). - Build daily_health_summary by selecting per-app, per-platform, per-day metrics and flags from the base: health_score, crash_rate_per_thousand, uninstall_rate_percentage, daily_average_rating, total_average_rating, rating_trend_7d, crash_rate_trend_7d, crash_rate_7d_avg, uninstall_rate_7d_avg, rating_7d_avg, crash_rate_30d_avg, installs_30d_sum, crashes_30d_sum, installs, uninstalls, total_activity, crash_count, volume_tier, health_status, and 0/1 flags: needs_immediate_attention, is_high_performing, is_declining_quality, is_stability_degrading. - Compute platform_health_comparison by grouping daily_health_summary by (date_day, platform) and deriving: total_apps = count distinct app_name; platform averages: health_score, crash_rate_7d_avg, uninstall_rate_7d_avg, rating_7d_avg; status distribution counts: excellent_apps, good_apps, average_apps, problematic_apps (Critical/High Risk/Poor Quality); attention/performance counts: high_volume_apps, apps_needing_attention, high_performing_apps; 30-day sums: platform_total_installs_30d, platform_total_crashes_30d, at_risk_installs_30d (from apps in Critical/High Risk). Aggregations ignore NULL inputs; distinct app_name eliminates duplicates. - Compute app_performance_ranking per (date_day, platform): health_rank = row_number ordered by health_score desc (higher is better); volume_rank = row_number ordered by installs_30d_sum desc; stability_rank = row_number ordered by crash_rate_30d_avg asc (lower crash rate is better); rating_rank = row_number ordered by rating_7d_avg desc. Ties are broken by engine-internal order (no explicit tie-breakers). Composite_performance_score (DOUBLE, no rounding) = 100 * [ 0.4 * (health_score / 100) + stability weight (0.3 if crash_rate_30d_avg <= 1; 0.2 if <= 5; 0.1 if <= 10; else 0) + satisfaction weight (0.2 if rating_7d_avg >= 4.5; 0.15 if >= 4.0; 0.1 if >= 3.5; 0.05 if >= 3.0; else 0) + volume weight (0.1 for High Volume; 0.075 for Medium Volume; 0.05 for Low Volume; 0.025 otherwise, covering Minimal Volume) ]. - Generate health_alerts only for rows where any is true: needs_immediate_attention = 1 OR health_score < 50 OR crash_rate_trend_7d > 5 OR rating_trend_7d < -0.3. For those rows: • alert_message and alert_severity use the first matching rule in this order: 1) crash_rate_trend_7d > 10 AND crash_rate_7d_avg > 5 → "CRITICAL: Crash rate spike detected" / CRITICAL 2) rating_trend_7d < -0.5 AND rating_7d_avg < 3.5 → "HIGH: Significant rating decline" / HIGH 3) uninstall_rate_7d_avg > 20 AND volume_tier in (''High Volume'',''Medium Volume'') → "HIGH: High uninstall rate for popular app" / HIGH 4) is_stability_degrading = 1 AND volume_tier = ''High Volume'' → "MEDIUM: Stability issues in high-volume app" / MEDIUM 5) is_declining_quality = 1 AND health_score < 60 → "MEDIUM: Quality decline trend" / MEDIUM 6) health_score < 40 → "LOW: Poor overall health score" / LOW else → NULL/NULL • recommended_action mapping (independent precedence): crash_rate_trend_7d > 10 → "Immediate investigation of crash causes required"; rating_trend_7d < -0.5 → "Review recent releases and user feedback"; uninstall_rate_7d_avg > 20 → "Analyze user retention and engagement strategies"; health_score < 40 → "Comprehensive health assessment and improvement plan needed"; else → "Continue monitoring". Rows not meeting the alert predicate produce NULL alert_* fields after the left join. - Final report: left join daily_health_summary to platform_health_comparison (on date_day, platform), app_performance_ranking (on date_day, app_name, platform), and health_alerts (on date_day, app_name, platform). Derive: • relative_platform_performance from (health_score vs platform_avg_health_score): > avg + 20 → "Above Average"; > avg → "Slightly Above Average"; > avg - 20 → "Below Average"; else → "Significantly Below Average". • overall_assessment (first matching rule): health_score >= 80 AND volume_tier = ''High Volume'' → "Star Performer - High quality, high volume"; health_score >= 70 AND crash_rate_7d_avg <= 5 → "Solid Performer - Good quality and stability"; health_score >= 50 AND volume_tier in (''High Volume'',''Medium Volume'') → "Average Performer - Monitor for improvements"; health_score < 50 OR alert_severity in (''CRITICAL'',''HIGH'') → "Needs Attention - Quality issues detected"; else → "Monitoring Required - Assess performance trends". • report_generated_at = current_timestamp (with time zone). Output one row per (date_day, app_name, platform). When rendering the query results, sort by date_day desc, platform, health_rank.'
      columns:
      - name: date_day
        data_type: DATE
        description: Calendar date of the metrics and assessments
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: app_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Application identifier/name as provided by the source
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: platform
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Source platform for the app metrics (e.g., google_play, apple_store)
        tests:
        - not_null
        - platform IN ('google_play', 'apple_store')
      - name: health_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: App health classification from the source; used in platform distributions and alert logic
        tests:
        - not_null
        - health_status IN ('Critical','High Risk','Poor Quality','Declining','Unstable','Excellent','Good','Average')
      - name: volume_tier
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'User volume tier used in scoring and alerts: High Volume, Medium Volume, Low Volume, Minimal Volume'
        tests:
        - not_null
        - volume_tier IN ('High Volume','Medium Volume','Low Volume','Minimal Volume')
      - name: health_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Composite health score from source (0–100 scale)
        tests:
        - not_null
        - health_score >= 0 AND health_score <= 100
      - name: crash_rate_per_thousand
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Current crash rate per 1,000 user interactions; non-negative; source value preserved
        tests:
        - crash_rate_per_thousand >= 0
      - name: crash_rate_7d_avg
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Rolling 7-day average crash rate (same unit as crash_rate_per_thousand); non-negative
        tests:
        - crash_rate_7d_avg >= 0
      - name: crash_rate_30d_avg
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Rolling 30-day average crash rate (same unit as crash_rate_per_thousand); non-negative
        tests:
        - crash_rate_30d_avg >= 0
      - name: uninstall_rate_percentage
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Current uninstall rate as percentage (0–100); source value preserved
        tests:
        - uninstall_rate_percentage >= 0 AND uninstall_rate_percentage <= 100
      - name: uninstall_rate_7d_avg
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Rolling 7-day average uninstall rate as percentage (0–100)
        tests:
        - uninstall_rate_7d_avg >= 0 AND uninstall_rate_7d_avg <= 100
      - name: daily_average_rating
        data_type: DECIMAL(10,2)
        description: Daily average user rating (1.00–5.00); two decimal places preserved
        tests:
        - daily_average_rating >= 1.00 AND daily_average_rating <= 5.00
      - name: rating_7d_avg
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Rolling 7-day average user rating (1.0–5.0) from source; double precision
        tests:
        - rating_7d_avg >= 1.0 AND rating_7d_avg <= 5.0
      - name: total_average_rating
        data_type: DECIMAL(10,2)
        description: Cumulative average user rating to date (1.00–5.00); two decimal places preserved
        tests:
        - total_average_rating >= 1.00 AND total_average_rating <= 5.00
      - name: rating_trend_7d
        data_type: DECIMAL(12,2)
        description: 7-day change in average rating (current minus prior), two decimal places; negative indicates decline
        tests:
        - rating_trend_7d >= -4.00 AND rating_trend_7d <= 4.00
      - name: crash_rate_trend_7d
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 7-day change in crash rate (same unit as crash_rate_per_thousand); positive indicates worsening
      - name: installs
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Daily install/download count; non-negative
        tests:
        - installs >= 0
      - name: installs_30d_sum
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: 30-day cumulative installs across the app; non-negative
        tests:
        - installs_30d_sum >= 0
      - name: crash_count
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Daily crash event count; non-negative
        tests:
        - crash_count >= 0
      - name: crashes_30d_sum
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: 30-day cumulative crash events across the app; non-negative
        tests:
        - crashes_30d_sum >= 0
      - name: total_activity
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Total daily user activity volume (source definition); non-negative
        tests:
        - total_activity >= 0
      - name: health_rank
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Rank within (date_day, platform) by health_score descending; 1 = best; ties broken by engine-internal order
        tests:
        - health_rank >= 1
      - name: volume_rank
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Rank within (date_day, platform) by installs_30d_sum descending; 1 = most installs; ties broken by engine-internal order
        tests:
        - volume_rank >= 1
      - name: stability_rank
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Rank within (date_day, platform) by crash_rate_30d_avg ascending; 1 = lowest crash rate; ties broken by engine-internal order
        tests:
        - stability_rank >= 1
      - name: rating_rank
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Rank within (date_day, platform) by rating_7d_avg descending; 1 = highest rating; ties broken by engine-internal order
        tests:
        - rating_rank >= 1
      - name: composite_performance_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Weighted composite score (0–100) from health, stability, satisfaction, and volume; no rounding
        tests:
        - composite_performance_score >= 0 AND composite_performance_score <= 100
      - name: platform_avg_health_score
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Platform daily average of health_score across distinct apps; 0–100; NULL if no platform aggregate
        tests:
        - platform_avg_health_score >= 0 AND platform_avg_health_score <= 100
      - name: platform_avg_crash_rate
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Platform daily average of crash_rate_7d_avg across apps (same unit as crash_rate_per_thousand)
        tests:
        - platform_avg_crash_rate >= 0
      - name: platform_avg_rating
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Platform daily average of rating_7d_avg across apps (1.0–5.0)
        tests:
        - platform_avg_rating >= 1.0 AND platform_avg_rating <= 5.0
      - name: platform_total_apps
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Distinct app count per platform per day used for context
        tests:
        - platform_total_apps >= 1
      - name: platform_problematic_apps
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Count of apps with health_status in ('Critical','High Risk','Poor Quality') per platform per day
        tests:
        - platform_problematic_apps >= 0
      - name: alert_message
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: First-matching alert text per defined precedence; NULL when no alert row joins
      - name: alert_severity
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Alert severity derived from rules: CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW; NULL when no alert row joins'
        tests:
        - alert_severity IN ('CRITICAL','HIGH','MEDIUM','LOW') OR alert_severity IS NULL
      - name: recommended_action
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Suggested remediation based on alert drivers; 'Continue monitoring' when alert predicate met but no specific driver; NULL when no alert row joins
      - name: needs_immediate_attention
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Urgency flag from source (0 = no, 1 = yes); used to include rows in alerts
        tests:
        - not_null
        - needs_immediate_attention IN (0,1)
      - name: is_high_performing
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Source flag indicating high-performing app (0/1)
        tests:
        - not_null
        - is_high_performing IN (0,1)
      - name: is_declining_quality
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Source flag indicating declining quality trend (0/1)
        tests:
        - not_null
        - is_declining_quality IN (0,1)
      - name: is_stability_degrading
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Source flag indicating degrading stability trend (0/1)
        tests:
        - not_null
        - is_stability_degrading IN (0,1)
      - name: relative_platform_performance
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Comparison vs platform_avg_health_score: Above/Slightly Above/Below/Significantly Below Average per defined thresholds'
        tests:
        - not_null
        - relative_platform_performance IN ('Above Average','Slightly Above Average','Below Average','Significantly Below Average')
      - name: overall_assessment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Final assessment derived by ordered rules from health_score, crash_rate_7d_avg, volume_tier, and alert_severity
        tests:
        - not_null
        - overall_assessment IN ('Star Performer - High quality, high volume','Solid Performer - Good quality and stability','Average Performer - Monitor for improvements','Needs Attention - Quality issues detected','Monitoring Required - Assess performance trends')
      - name: report_generated_at
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Timestamp of report creation using current_timestamp (session time zone)
        tests:

version: "1.0"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# PHASE 2: Defines the business logic from staging tables to analytical models. #
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
modeling_spec:
  purpose: "Transform staging data into business-ready analytical models that provide deep insights into app performance, user behavior, and revenue optimization across Google Play and Apple Store platforms."
  
  design_principles:
    intermediate_purpose: "Create reusable, business-centric data models that consolidate platform-specific data and apply complex business logic for downstream consumption."
    marts_purpose: "Deliver analysis-ready fact tables and dimensional models optimized for business intelligence, reporting, and data science applications."
    grain_importance: "Every model must have an explicitly defined grain to ensure consistent aggregation and prevent double-counting in downstream analysis."
    cross_platform_consistency: "Harmonize metrics and dimensions across Google Play and Apple Store to enable unified cross-platform analytics."

  intermediate_models:
    - name: int_user_lifecycle_analysis
      description: App-level lifecycle classifications per active day and platform derived from store installs/downloads, with rolling activity windows, status, value segment, and data quality flag
      grain: One or more rows per package_name × platform × date_day with activity_metric > 0 and first_install_date <= date_day; if a package_name exists in both sources, there can be duplicate rows per distinct first_install_date
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_google_play__stats_installs_overview (date_day, package_name, device_installs)
      - staging.stg_apple_store__app_store_download_standard_daily (date_day, app_name, total_downloads)
      business_logic: '- Build user_first_install: - From Google Play, take the earliest date_day per package_name where device_installs > 0. - From Apple Store, take the earliest date_day per app_name (renamed to package_name) where total_downloads > 0. - Combine both sets without de-duplication, so a package present in both sources yields two first_install_date records. - Build daily_active_users: - Google Play: date_day, package_name, platform = "google_play", is_active = 1 if device_installs > 0 else 0, activity_metric = device_installs. - Apple Store: date_day, app_name as package_name, platform = "apple_store", is_active = 1 if total_downloads > 0 else 0, activity_metric = total_downloads. - Union all rows from both sources. - Join daily_active_users to user_first_install on package_name only (platform is not used in the join), then keep rows where is_active = 1. This can duplicate active rows when both sources contribute a first_install_date for the same package_name. - Within each package_name and platform, ordered by date_day, compute: - user_age_days = difference in days between first_install_date and date_day. - active_days_l7 = rolling count of the most recent up to 7 active rows (not calendar days); duplicates from the join are treated as separate rows. - active_days_l30 = rolling count of the most recent up to 30 active rows (not calendar days); duplicates from the join are treated as separate rows. - last_active_date = the previous active date_day within the same package_name and platform (based on active rows only). - Classify: - user_lifecycle_stage by user_age_days: <=7 New User; <=30 Growing User; <=90 Established User; <=365 Mature User; else Veteran User. - user_activity_level by active_days_l7: >=6 Highly Active; >=3 Moderately Active; >=1 Low Active; else Inactive (does not occur because only active rows are kept). - user_status by age and gap from last_active_date: if user_age_days <= 1 then New User; else if no prior active date or the gap is <= 1 day then Continuous User; else if gap <= 7 days then Returning User; else if gap <= 30 days then Reactivated User; else Long Dormant User. - user_value_segment by active_days_l30 and user_age_days: if active_days_l30 >= 25 and age >= 30 then High Value; else if active_days_l30 >= 15 and age >= 7 then Medium Value; else if active_days_l30 >= 5 then Low Value; else Potential Churn. - Final outputs and flags: - is_new_user = 1 if user_lifecycle_stage is New User else 0. - is_returning_user = 1 if user_status is Returning User else 0. - is_reactivated_user = 1 if user_status is Reactivated User else 0. - is_at_risk = 1 if user_value_segment is Potential Churn else 0. - data_quality_flag: Invalid Activity if activity_metric < 0; Invalid User Age if user_age_days < 0; Invalid Install Date if first_install_date > date_day; else Valid. - Apply a final filter user_age_days >= 0, which removes rows with negative or null age and, combined with is_active = 1, means invalid flags do not appear in the final result.'
      columns:
      - name: date_day
        data_type: DATE
        description: Calendar date of the retained active row (activity_metric > 0)
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: package_name
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: App identifier; Apple app_name is mapped into this field
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: platform
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Source platform label derived from the dataset ('google_play' or 'apple_store')
        tests:
        - not_null
        - platform IN ('google_play', 'apple_store')
      - name: user_lifecycle_stage
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Stage by user_age_days: <=7 New; <=30 Growing; <=90 Established; <=365 Mature; else Veteran'
        tests:
        - not_null
        - user_lifecycle_stage IN ('New User', 'Growing User', 'Established User', 'Mature User', 'Veteran User')
      - name: user_activity_level
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Engagement by active_days_l7: >=6 Highly Active; >=3 Moderately Active; >=1 Low Active; else Inactive (inactive does not occur because only active rows are kept)'
        tests:
        - not_null
        - user_activity_level IN ('Highly Active', 'Moderately Active', 'Low Active', 'Inactive')
      - name: user_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Status by age and gap from last_active_date: age<=1 New; no prior active date or gap<=1 Continuous; gap<=7 Returning; gap<=30 Reactivated; else Long Dormant'
        tests:
        - not_null
        - user_status IN ('New User', 'Continuous User', 'Returning User', 'Reactivated User', 'Long Dormant User')
      - name: user_value_segment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Value segment by active_days_l30 and age: >=25 and age>=30 High; >=15 and age>=7 Medium; >=5 Low; else Potential Churn'
        tests:
        - not_null
        - user_value_segment IN ('High Value', 'Medium Value', 'Low Value', 'Potential Churn')
      - name: user_age_days
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Days between first_install_date and date_day; filtered to >= 0 in the final output
        tests:
        - not_null
        - user_age_days >= 0
      - name: active_days_l7
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Rolling count of the most recent up to 7 active rows within each package_name and platform; values in [1,7]
        tests:
        - not_null
        - active_days_l7 >= 1
        - active_days_l7 <= 7
      - name: active_days_l30
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Rolling count of the most recent up to 30 active rows within each package_name and platform; values in [1,30]
        tests:
        - not_null
        - active_days_l30 >= 1
        - active_days_l30 <= 30
      - name: activity_metric
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Raw daily installs/downloads from the source (device_installs or total_downloads); strictly > 0 in the final output
        tests:
        - not_null
        - activity_metric > 0
      - name: first_install_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: Earliest observed install/download date per source for the package_name; packages present in both sources can have two dates, which can duplicate rows when joined on package_name only
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: is_new_user
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 1 if user_lifecycle_stage = 'New User', else 0
        tests:
        - not_null
        - is_new_user IN (0, 1)
      - name: is_returning_user
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 1 if user_status = 'Returning User', else 0
        tests:
        - not_null
        - is_returning_user IN (0, 1)
      - name: is_reactivated_user
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 1 if user_status = 'Reactivated User', else 0

        - is_reactivated_user IN (0, 1)
      - name: is_at_risk
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 1 if user_value_segment = 'Potential Churn', else 0
        tests:
        - not_null
        - is_at_risk IN (0, 1)
      - name: data_quality_flag
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Quality status: ''Invalid Activity'' if activity_metric < 0; ''Invalid User Age'' if user_age_days < 0; ''Invalid Install Date'' if first_install_date > date_day; else ''Valid'' (final filter removes invalid cases)'
        tests:
        - not_null
        - data_quality_flag IN ('Valid', 'Invalid Activity', 'Invalid User Age', 'Invalid Install Date')
    - name: int_user_rfm_analysis
      description: User value analysis by RFM over Google Play earnings (USD) with one row per app-country-currency and deterministic scoring and flags
      grain: One row per app_id, buyer_country, buyer_currency
      source_models:
      - staging.stg_google_play__earnings
      business_logic: '- Input extraction (user_transaction_base): - Read rows from staging.stg_google_play__earnings where date_day and revenue_usd are not null. - Map fields: transaction_date is date_day cast to date; app_id from package_name; buyer_country from country; buyer_currency; transaction_amount from revenue_usd. - Set transaction_type = ''Purchase'' and refund_type = ''NONE'' for all rows. - net_revenue equals revenue_usd if positive, otherwise 0; valid_transaction equals 1 if revenue_usd > 0, otherwise 0. - Aggregation (user_aggregations), grouped by (app_id, buyer_country, buyer_currency); keep only groups with at least one valid transaction: - recency_days: days from the most recent transaction date to the current date. - frequency_count: number of valid transactions (revenue_usd > 0). - monetary_value: sum of net_revenue in USD (two decimals). - first_transaction_date: earliest transaction_date; last_transaction_date: latest transaction_date. - total_transactions: count of all rows in the group (including non-positive revenue). - avg_transaction_value: average net_revenue over all rows in the group (zeros included); double precision, no rounding applied. - subscription_count: number of subscription-type transactions; always 0 in this model. - purchase_count: number of purchase-type transactions; equals total_transactions here. - refund_count: number of full refunds; always 0 in this model. - customer_lifetime_days: days between the first and last transaction dates (non-negative). - Scoring (rfm_quartiles): - recency_score: 4 if recency_days ≤ 30; 3 if ≤ 90; 2 if ≤ 180; else 1. - frequency_score: 4 if frequency_count ≥ 10; 3 if ≥ 5; 2 if ≥ 2; else 1. - monetary_score: 4 if monetary_value ≥ 500; 3 if ≥ 200; 2 if ≥ 50; else 1. - Quartiles (not used in final output) computed over all groups: recency quartiles by sorting recency_days from largest to smallest; frequency and monetary quartiles by sorting values from smallest to largest. - Segmentation and derived metrics (rfm_segments): - rfm_score = recency_score + frequency_score + monetary_score (range 3–12). - rfm_segment_code: three-character string formed by the recency, frequency, and monetary scores (e.g., "444"). - customer_segment (first-match order): - Champions: recency_score ≥ 3 AND frequency_score ≥ 3 AND monetary_score ≥ 3 - Loyal Customers: recency_score ≥ 3 AND frequency_score ≥ 2 AND monetary_score ≥ 2 - Potential Loyalists: recency_score ≥ 3 AND frequency_score ≤ 2 AND monetary_score ≥ 3 - New Customers: recency_score ≥ 3 AND frequency_score ≤ 2 AND monetary_score ≤ 2 - At Risk: recency_score = 2 AND frequency_score ≥ 3 AND monetary_score ≥ 3 - Cannot Lose Them: recency_score = 2 AND frequency_score ≥ 2 AND monetary_score ≥ 2 - Hibernating: recency_score ≤ 2 AND frequency_score ≥ 2 AND monetary_score ≥ 3 - Lost: recency_score ≤ 1 AND frequency_score ≥ 2 AND monetary_score ≤ 2 - Others: all remaining cases - estimated_clv (USD): annualized revenue = (monetary_value divided by customer_lifetime_days) times 365 when lifetime_days > 0; otherwise equals monetary_value; double precision, no rounding. - customer_health_status (first-match order): Healthy if recency_days ≤ 30 and frequency_count ≥ 5; Stable if recency_days ≤ 90 and frequency_count ≥ 2; At Risk if recency_days ≤ 180; otherwise Critical. - Final selection and flags (final): - is_high_value_customer = 1 if customer_segment is Champions or Loyal Customers; otherwise 0. - is_churn_risk = 1 if customer_health_status is Critical; otherwise 0. - is_recent_customer = 1 if recency_days ≤ 7; otherwise 0. - data_quality_flag (first-match order): Invalid Recency if recency_days < 0; Invalid Frequency if frequency_count ≤ 0; Invalid Monetary if monetary_value < 0; Invalid Date Range if first_transaction_date > last_transaction_date; otherwise Valid. - Keep only rows with recency_days ≥ 0, frequency_count > 0, and monetary_value ≥ 0. - analysis_timestamp set to the current execution timestamp (time zone aware); same value for all rows within one run. - Grain: - One output row per (app_id, buyer_country, buyer_currency); all metrics computed from the above rules.'
      columns:
      - name: app_id
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Application identifier sourced from package_name; grouping key component
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: buyer_country
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: ISO 2-letter country code sourced from country; grouping key component
        tests:
        - LENGTH(buyer_country) = 2
      - name: buyer_currency
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: ISO 3-letter currency code; grouping key component
        tests:
        - LENGTH(buyer_currency) = 3
      - name: recency_days
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Days between the most recent transaction date and the current date; non-negative in final output
        tests:
        - not_null
        - recency_days >= 0
      - name: frequency_count
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Number of valid transactions (revenue_usd > 0) per group; strictly > 0
        tests:
        - not_null
        - frequency_count > 0
      - name: monetary_value
        data_type: DECIMAL(38,2)
        description: Sum of net revenue (USD), where each row's net revenue equals revenue_usd if positive else 0; non-negative
        tests:
        - not_null
        - monetary_value >= 0
      - name: first_transaction_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: Earliest transaction date in the group
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: last_transaction_date
        data_type: DATE
        description: Latest transaction date in the group
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: total_transactions
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Total rows per group including non-positive revenue
        tests:
        - not_null
        - total_transactions >= frequency_count
      - name: avg_transaction_value
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: Average net revenue per row in the group, including zeros; no rounding
        tests:
        - avg_transaction_value >= 0
      - name: subscription_count
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Number of subscription-type transactions; always 0 in this model
        tests:
        - subscription_count >= 0
      - name: purchase_count
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Number of purchase-type transactions; equals total_transactions in this model
        tests:
        - purchase_count >= 0
      - name: refund_count
        data_type: HUGEINT
        description: Number of full refunds; always 0 in this model
        tests:
        - refund_count >= 0
      - name: customer_lifetime_days
        data_type: BIGINT
        description: Days between the first and last transaction dates; non-negative
        tests:
        - customer_lifetime_days >= 0
      - name: recency_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'RFM recency score: 4 if ≤30d, 3 if ≤90d, 2 if ≤180d, else 1'
        tests:
        - not_null
        - recency_score BETWEEN 1 AND 4
      - name: frequency_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'RFM frequency score: 4 if ≥10, 3 if ≥5, 2 if ≥2, else 1'
        tests:
        - not_null
        - frequency_score BETWEEN 1 AND 4
      - name: monetary_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 'RFM monetary score: 4 if ≥500 USD, 3 if ≥200, 2 if ≥50, else 1'
        tests:
        - not_null
        - monetary_score BETWEEN 1 AND 4
      - name: rfm_score
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: Sum of the three RFM scores; range 3–12
        tests:
        - not_null
        - rfm_score BETWEEN 3 AND 12
      - name: rfm_segment_code
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Three-digit string formed by recency_score, frequency_score, and monetary_score (e.g., '444')
        tests:
        - not_null
        - LENGTH(rfm_segment_code) = 3
      - name: customer_segment
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: Segment label assigned by the ordered RFM rules listed in the business logic
        tests:
        - not_null
        - customer_segment IN ('Champions','Loyal Customers','Potential Loyalists','New Customers','At Risk','Cannot Lose Them','Hibernating','Lost','Others')
      - name: estimated_clv
        data_type: DOUBLE
        description: 'Annualized revenue estimate: average daily revenue times 365 if lifetime_days>0, else equals monetary_value; no rounding'
        tests:
        - estimated_clv >= 0
      - name: customer_health_status
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Health status derived from recency_days and frequency_count: Healthy, Stable, At Risk, or Critical'
        tests:
        - not_null
        - customer_health_status IN ('Healthy','Stable','At Risk','Critical')
      - name: is_high_value_customer
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 1 if customer_segment is Champions or Loyal Customers, else 0
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: is_churn_risk
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 1 if customer_health_status is Critical, else 0
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: is_recent_customer
        data_type: INTEGER
        description: 1 if recency_days ≤ 7, else 0
        tests:
        - not_null
      - name: data_quality_flag
        data_type: VARCHAR
        description: 'Quality flag from ordered checks: Invalid Recency, Invalid Frequency, Invalid Monetary, Invalid Date Range, else Valid'
        tests:
        - not_null
        - data_quality_flag IN ('Valid','Invalid Recency','Invalid Frequency','Invalid Monetary','Invalid Date Range')
      - name: analysis_timestamp
        data_type: TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
        description: Execution timestamp for the run; identical across rows within a run and time zone aware
        tests:
